text:
The Lightning are 15-5-2 with Nikita Kucherov's trade request hanging over every one of those games. The Associated Press reported on Oct. 30 that he told the club he won't re-sign and wants out, and general manager Julien Brisebois has said publicly he has no intention of moving him. Kucherov's answer, so far, was a hat trick against Buffalo.

The awkward part for anyone hoping this blows up: the hockey is excellent. Tampa has 55% of the expected goals, the quality of chances, and Daily Faceoff Edmonton called them ruthless at 5-on-5 before Thursday's 3-1 win over the Oilers. Brayden Point is back from injured reserve, and his line with Kucherov and Jake Guentzel has outscored opponents 11-2. The Zemgus Girgensons, Pontus Holmberg and Ilya Mikheyev checking line is 11-5, which is how you beat teams on nights the stars are quiet.

Some of it is running hot. Our numbers have them about four points ahead of their play, and John Carlson has 14 points in his last 10 games against 7.9 expected. Carlson and Charle-Edouard D'Astous have controlled 65% of the chances together, so the process is real even if the pace isn't.

Their playoff chances sit at 97%, with a 54% shot at the Atlantic. Rookie Sam O'Reilly scored his first NHL goal this week. The thing to watch isn't the standings; it's whether Brisebois's stance holds as the trade deadline gets closer.
headline: Winning loud with a trade request in the room
